source.title: GLBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Graph with Large Language Models
source.authors: Yuhan Li; Peisong Wang; Xiao Zhu; Aochuan Chen; Haiyun Jiang; Deng Cai; Victor Wai Kin Chan; Jia Li

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines model-size scaling for graph node-classification performance, not held-out language-model pretraining loss, extrapolation of that loss, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its findings concern a related but different construct.
record.gate_note: The paper reports accuracy sweeps for GraphLLM methods and concludes that their performance does not show clear scaling laws. These are downstream graph-classification accuracies, not the loss or allocation measures named by the claim versions; the findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: Appendix D.2 varies the language-model encoder size (4M to 13B) with the GNN fixed and reports downstream Cora node-classification accuracy. That bears on V6 (downstream performance vs scale) in a new setting. The sweep mixes model families (TinyBERT, BERT, Sentence-BERT, RoBERTa, LLaMA2) rather than controlled scaling, so it is weak evidence. The GNN-size sweep (D.1) scales a non-language model on accuracy, not loss, so it fits no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude no obvious or clear model-scaling law exists for current GraphLLM methods, for either GNN or LLM component scaling, on their benchmark.
record.recipe_differences: This is a graph node-classification benchmark using accuracy sweeps on OFA and GLEM, rather than a language-model pretraining loss study or a compute-optimal allocation experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The study varies GNN depth, units per layer, and LLM backbone size; it reports no significant improvement trend for the tested GNN-scale sweep and no steady accuracy increase across LLM sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: For OFA and GLEM on Cora, scaling GNN depth/width (0.6M-90M params) with a fixed Sentence-BERT encoder gives no consistent accuracy gain for GLEM (R² about 0). OFA shows modest within-depth gains (about 64 to 75).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream accuracy of GNN components in GraphLLM pipelines does not reliably improve with GNN parameter count.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2024 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
record.problems: The scaling experiments are on Cora and report graph-classification accuracy rather than held-out language-model pretraining loss. The checklist states that error bars were not reported.
record.rows_left_out: The individual numeric entries in Table 9 and Table 10 are not separately listed; the rows record the authors' stated sweep-level findings. They do not correspond to claim-version measures.

untested.parts: No fitted law extrapolated to larger runs.
No fixed-parameter-count shape comparison for language models. The GNN depth/width sweep varies parameter count and measures accuracy.
No loss power-law fits in other modalities or regimes.
No fitted exponents or comparison of fitting choices.
Only one dataset (Cora), one task, no seeds or error bars; no relation to pretraining loss tested.

missing.what: Per-model numeric accuracies for the LM-size sweep (OFA GNN; GLEM GNN and LLM classifiers), including OOM entries for LLaMA2 under GLEM
Main-text cross-method observation: 7B-LLM methods (ENGINE, InstructGLM, GraphText) do not beat 110M-scale methods. This is confounded by method differences.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6/discusses gate is too strict for the LM-encoder sweep, which measures downstream accuracy against LM size. That is V6's construct, though in a confounded, single-dataset setting, so the evidence is weak. Data scaling was not studied. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling in language models.
Prediction of much larger runs' held-out pretraining loss from smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Architecture effects at a fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss scaling in other modalities or training regimes.
Predictability of downstream task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting/setup choices, and departures of loss curves from a single power law.

rows.subject: OFA
rows.size_stated: GNN parameter counts from 592769 to 44856321 in the reported sweep
rows.operation_detail: Varied GNN depth and units per layer with SentenceBERT fixed; evaluated Cora accuracy.
rows.value: No significant trend of improvement as the number of parameters increases.
rows.note: The text summarizes the sweep rather than reporting a single aggregate accuracy. The measure is graph-classification accuracy, not held-out pretraining loss.
rows.check: GNN width/depth scaling with downstream accuracy. This is not a language model and not a loss measure, so no version applies. Table 9 numbers exist (OFA 4-layer 66.10 to 72.97 across 0.59M to 32M params), and Figure 4 shows high R² within depth for OFA.

rows.subject: GLEM
rows.size_stated: GNN parameter counts from 66966165 to 90033429 in the reported sweep
rows.operation_detail: Varied GNN depth and units per layer with SentenceBERT fixed; evaluated GNN and LLM classifier accuracy on Cora.
rows.value: No significant trend of improvement as the number of parameters increases.
rows.note: The text summarizes the sweep rather than reporting a single aggregate accuracy. The measure is graph-classification accuracy, not held-out pretraining loss.
rows.check: GNN scaling with a fixed LLM is not a language-model scale sweep. GLEM accuracy is flat (GNN about 79-82, LLM about 71-74; R² about 0). Keep under fits_no_version.

rows.subject: OFA
rows.operation_detail: Varied the LLM backbone size with fixed GNNs; evaluated Cora accuracy.
rows.value: Increasing LLM scale had a less noticeable impact; performance did not increase steadily with parameter count. OFA with LLaMA2-13B achieved the best results, while OFA with RoBERTa-large achieved 58.3% Accuracy.
rows.note: The paper gives these as graph-classification accuracies and describes the broader sweep qualitatively; this is not a held-out pretraining-loss measure.
rows.check: This bears on V6 (encoder LM size vs downstream accuracy). Table 10 OFA: TinyBERT 56.33, BERT-base 65.52, BERT-large 65.18, Sent-BERT-small 78.97, Sent-BERT 75.24, RoBERTa-base 56.00, RoBERTa-large 58.03, LLaMA2-7B 78.72, LLaMA2-13B 80.56. The largest model is best, but the trend is non-monotonic. The text's '58.3%' mis-transcribes the table's 58.03. The baseline should be the TinyBERT 4M entry.

rows.subject: GLEM
rows.operation_detail: Varied the LLM backbone size with fixed GNNs; evaluated Cora accuracy.
rows.value: Increasing LLM scale had a less noticeable impact on model performance.
rows.note: The paper's summary concerns graph-classification accuracy; the table also reports OOM entries for some configurations.
rows.check: This bears on V6. GLEM (GNN/LLM classifier): TinyBERT 72.15/37.52, BERT-base 81.57/73.11, then flat or declining (BERT-large 79.06/70.60, RoBERTa-large 79.26/72.53). LLaMA2 sizes are OOM. The row should record these numbers rather than only the qualitative summary.

relationships.condition: GraphLLM methods (OFA, GLEM) on Cora node classification, LM encoders 4M-13B from mixed families, GNN fixed
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises from smallest to largest encoder but not steadily (r3, r4). BERT-large ≤ BERT-base; RoBERTa-large 58.03 vs Sent-BERT-small 78.97 for OFA; GLEM plateaus after 109M. Single dataset, no error bars, family confounded with size.
relationships.display_finding: OFA scored 58.03 with RoBERTa-large versus 78.97 with Sent-BERT-small, BERT-large did no better than BERT-base, and GLEM plateaued after 109M; overall endpoint gains were confounded by encoder-family differences and lacked error bars.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
